tagline: See what a command will change before it runs

features.title: Hold
features.detail: A risky Bash command waits before it runs, with no timeout: every check of your block-destructive hook (rm, git reset --hard, force push, SQL DROP, production deploys, gcloud, az, databricks, chmod 777, curl into a shell, credential reads) plus mv over a file, > over a file and Windows deletes.

features.title: Your rules
features.detail: ~/.claude/mods-data/mod-blast-radius/rules.json, an array of { "pattern": "regex", "reason": "text", "flags": "i" }. Read again when the file changes. A bad entry is skipped with a note in the settings pane; the built-in checks never depend on it.

features.title: One prompt
features.detail: After you press Run, the settings hook's own Destructive operation ask is answered, so you are not asked twice. Any other ask or deny passes through.

features.title: No drawing surface
features.detail: In a VS Code chat panel, claude -p or an SDK session nothing can show the hold, so the call is not held: the permission system asks instead, with the reason.

features.title: Preview
features.detail: Paths with counts and size, git status and dry runs, the commits a force push would drop. Read-only: the command itself never runs.

features.title: Run or Cancel
features.detail: Cancel refuses the call with a reason Claude reads. A narrow terminal draws the same report above the prompt.

spans.text: runs at once, nothing is held
